feed.title: NPR Programs: All Things Considered
feed.subtitle: All Things Considered hosts Ailsa Chang, Mary Louise Kelly, Juana Summers and Scott Detrow present the program's trademark mix of news, interviews, commentaries, reviews, and offbeat features 7 days a week.

entry.title: The questions swirling around a U.K. base and possible Iranian-backed attacks
entry.summary: British police said they had made a seventh arrest in a murky plot that may have targeted a U.K. airbase.

entry.title: CDC funding for HIV prevention shifted from providers to states under Trump
entry.summary: Nonprofits fighting HIV used get direct funding from the CDC. Now that money is going to state health departments that may have other priorities.

entry.title: Warm ocean waters may have led to first known sea turtle nesting in California
entry.summary: NPR's Ailsa Chang talks with marine ecologist Jeff Seminoff about the first known natural sea turtle nesting on California's shores.

entry.title: Cubans in U.S. sour on Trump's immigration policies
entry.summary: Cubans in the U.S. are growing frustrated with President Trump's immigration policies, which has resulted in their detention and the dismissal of protections that have benefitted Cubans specifically.

entry.title: Journalist April Ryan's new memoir explores 'Blacklash' and threats to free press
entry.summary: NPR's Juana Summers speaks to White House correspondent April Ryan about her new memoir, Notes on a Blacklash: When a Black Woman Goes Viral.

entry.title: Jim Bakker moved millions — of dollars and followers — with his TV ministry
entry.summary: NPR's Sacha Pfeiffer talks with Dartmouth College religion professor Randall Balmer about Jim Bakker's legacy.

entry.title: An early start to flu season moves up vaccination timing
entry.summary: This year's flu season is unusual. It started early and in the West, instead of the South. A new variant with a mutation that helps the virus evade immunity may be playing a role.

entry.title: In final weeks, campaign spending ramps up as competitive electoral map comes into focus
entry.summary: With four weeks to go until Election Day, the map for competitive House and Senate races is coming into focus as Democrats try to capitalize on any advantage.

entry.title: Trump says Fort Hood shooter can be executed by firing squad
entry.summary: The last time the U.S. military held an execution was in 1961, by hanging. The last military execution by firing squad was in 1945, when an American soldier was shot for desertion in World War II.

entry.title: A new executive order aims to bring down diesel prices. Could it work?
entry.summary: President Trump has signed an executive order that would allow anyone to purchase a tax-free type of fuel known as red-dyed diesel. This could save truckers money, but it's not always an option.
